Even with official plating and max dura, this boat does not have enough dura to survive against a true battle ship. I believe this boat is a clipper-killer that would be very good at running away from the big battle boats and rowboats.

comments.author: Misun
comments.body:
I think the point that he is trying to make with EA, is that all important start-of-combat ramp up. If you can build up speed early on in the fight, you can keep your distance quite easily. After that you can switch it off until you need to put some distance between yourself and a pursuer that may be catching up.

I do agree that the dura kind of makes less sense, since you will be working to avoid getting within cannon16 kill range like crazy, if you screw up and let yourself get caught in that zone, even at max dura you will be hard pressed to survive.

comments.author: Liza
comments.body:
Guys, This isn't a true battle ship. It just does not have the dura to go toe-to-toe with a true battle ship. That "excessive wr" is so that under any conditions you can reach maximum speed. Plain and simple this is a pirate boat, not a maritimer's boat. So even if you are loaded down with goods and provisions you can still chase if need be or run if need be.

I think people who are wanting to make one of these and then setting it up against a FIS or even a FCV are going to be disappointed in the outcome. Turn is great if you can get it, but even with max turn you will lose all your speed eventually with all the turning you do in battle, so I really dont' think turning EA on and off in a battle situation is going to do what you think it will. Plus what skill do you keep turned off so that you can constantly turn that one on? Are you really thinking you will have time to turn another skill off, turn EA on, turn it back off, then turn that other skill back on again?
